### Salary prediction with PySpark ML

[Big Data and Cloud Analytics, Boston University, 2026]{.meta}

Predicted annual salary for 9,300 US job postings with Spark on AWS EC2. I rebuilt the salary target from mixed hourly and annual pay, extracted required experience from posting text, and compared linear, polynomial and random forest models.

- Random forest: test R² 0.54, RMSE about \$46,000
- Experience has a strongly diminishing return, flattening after about 12 years
- Diagnosed and avoided the perfect multicollinearity in the starter template

**Tools:** PySpark MLlib, AWS EC2, Python, Seaborn, Quarto
:::
:::

::: {.project}
![Top 10 features by random forest importance](images/rf_feature_importance.png){fig-alt="Bar chart of random forest feature importance, led by experience at 52.7 percent and education level at 18.9 percent"}

::: {}
### What drives pay in job postings

[Big Data and Cloud Analytics, Boston University, 2026]{.meta}

Feature importance from the random forest model. Required experience explains just over half of the model's predictive power, followed by education level and occupation group, with computing roles paying the most.

The regression models agree on the same drivers and add direction and size: about \$19,000 for the first year of experience, falling to about \$4,000 by year ten.
:::
:::

### Career market analysis: securities and investments

[Group project, Big Data and Cloud Analytics, Boston University, 2026]{.meta}

Analysed 7,074 job postings in the US securities and investments industry to identify the skills, locations and role variants that open entry into business intelligence and data analyst careers. I led site structure, integration and publishing, and documented four data defects we found and repaired in the source data.

[Visit the project website](https://fuadbbv.github.io/ad688-career-evaluation-group1/){.btn .btn-cv}
:::
